human_tolerance.notes: Common in farm ponds, ditches, borrow pits and roadside water anywhere east of the Mississippi, and widely farmed and eaten. 'Adult frogs try to escape by splashing and leaping into deep water.'

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: The breeding season lasts two to three months; males take up calling territories 3 to 6 m apart in shallow water and choruses form and break up repeatedly.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: Outside the breeding season, foraging at the margins of ponds and ditches.

vocalizations.description: The bull-like bellow the male gives from a calling territory, which gives the species its name. Males also give separate territorial calls as threats and encounter calls before combat, and subordinate 'silent males' give none at all.
A piercing scream from a trapped individual, which may surprise an attacker enough for the frog to escape; an attack on one bullfrog alerts others nearby to retreat into deeper water.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared nocturnal-anuran program; the temperature window brackets the 15 degrees Celsius below which development ceases and the 32 degrees Celsius above which development goes abnormal, and the calling months cover the southern breeding season.

external.note: GBIF usage key 2427091 from the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy, which accepts Lithobates catesbeianus and holds Rana catesbeiana as a synonym; iNaturalist taxon id 65979. No Wikidata id is recorded rather than guess one.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Native to the eastern United States, widely farmed and introduced for food and pest control; the escape behaviour is from Wikipedia. The rest are judgements.

habitat.resources.note: The food resources follow the diet shares, with the 0.25 fish share folded into small_vertebrate because the schema's resource-tag list has no fish tag; pond is authored from the breeding and escape behaviour.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Deep water and the vegetated margin of a pond or ditch.

habitat.use.note: Shares authored: most of its time is in or at the edge of water, with foraging excursions onto land.

look.note: Olive-green dorsal surface, plain or mottled and banded with greyish brown, an off-white underside blotched with yellow or grey, a prominent tympanum behind the eye and a yellow gular in territorial males; proportions and palette are authored.

range.note: 'Originally native to eastern North America ... found in every U.S. state east of the Mississippi River', from the Maritimes west to Idaho and Texas. The introduced list is the set of places named in the article: western United States states, Hawaii, nearly every Mexican state, and Belgium, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, Haiti, Italy, Jamaica, the Netherlands, Puerto Rico, the United Kingdom, Argentina, Brazil, China, Colombia, Japan, South Korea, Uruguay and Venezuela.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Eggs 'hatch in three to five days' and 'time to metamorphosis ranges from a few months in the southern part of the range'; the stage durations are read off those.

seasonal.phases.note: A breeding season of two to three months with males arriving in late May or early June and remaining into July is from Wikipedia; the phase dates are widened to cover the southern part of the range.

seasonal.strategy.note: No dormancy is described; 'the reproductive cycle of American bullfrogs in Oregon is mainly restricted to the summer season', so the species is active year-round in the southern United States.

traits.defense.note: 'Adult frogs try to escape by splashing and leaping into deep water. A trapped individual may squawk or emit a piercing scream.'

traits.diet.note: Weights authored from 'a generalist carnivore, consuming a wide variety of prey': rodents, lizards, snakes, other frogs, crayfish, small birds, scorpions, tarantulas and bats, plus 'a large percentage of aquatic animals, such as fish, tadpoles' and invertebrates such as snails, worms and insects.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of the 3.6-6 in (about 9-15 cm) snout-to-vent length.

traits.lifespan_y.note: 'Maximum lifespan in the wild is estimated to be 8 to 10 years, but one frog lived for almost 16 years in captivity.'

traits.locomotion_modes.note: It walks, hops and swims; 'adult frogs try to escape by splashing and leaping into deep water' and newly hatched tadpoles 'prefer to live in shallow water'.

traits.mass_kg.note: 0.35 kg is the midpoint of the adult span the article gives: a frog gains weight 'from 5 to 175 g' in its first eight months and 'large, mature individuals can weigh up to 500 g', with 800 g recorded exceptionally.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: 0.175-0.5 kg, the weight reached at eight months up to the recorded maximum for large mature individuals.

traits.nest_type.note: 'The female chooses a site in shallow water among vegetation, and lays a batch of up to 20,000 eggs' as a floating sheet, so no nest is built and None is recorded.

traits.social.note: 'Male bullfrogs aggregate into groups called choruses', with males spaced 3 to 6 m apart as territorial, flocking or satellite males.

traits.wariness.note: It is found in farm ponds and ditches across its native range and is heavily harvested; 0.2 is a judgement.

vocalizations.croak.note: 'At least three different types of calls have been noted in male bullfrogs under different circumstances ... territorial calls made as threats to other males, advertisement calls made to attract females, and encounter calls which precede combat.'

vocalizations.scream.note: 'A trapped individual may squawk or emit a piercing scream, which may surprise the attacker sufficiently for the frog to escape.'
